newsitem.title: USA: Minn. board to serve as conduit for hospital bonds.
newsitem.headline: Minn. board to serve as conduit for hospital bonds.

text.p: The Minnesota Agricultural and Economic Development Board on Wednesday gave final approval to serve as a conduit to sell $175 million of tax-exempt bonds for a not-for-profit health system based in Minneapolis, a system spokeswoman said.

The board voted 7-0 to serve as the issuing authority for the Fairview Health System, which plans to use the proceeds to fund acquisition of the former University of Minnesota Hospital and clinic in Minneapolis, health facilities around the state and other projects, Fairview spokeswoman Jean Tracy said.
About $87.5 of the proceeds will be used to pay off a promissary note Fairview issued for the university hospital acquisitions. That note is due to expire on June 30.
Another $23 million will fund capital improvements at Fairview-University Medical Center and $27 million will go to construction of a new health care facility in Wyoming, Minn., Tracy said.
Other proceeds will be used for debt refinancing and smaller capital projects, Tracy said.
Fairview anticipates closing on the issue April 24, Tracy said. Smith Barney Inc has been tapped as senior manager for the deal and the bonds will be insured through MBIA Insurance Corp, Tracy said.

Fairview turned to the board in February after a Minneapolis City Council committee rejected the deal due to union pressure. The American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees represented university hospital employees until Fairview acquired the facility in January.
AFSCME has filed a petition with the National Labor Relations Board to again represent the employees.
